Subject: Production latency & 5xx spike — Reserved throughput not honored (PO on hold)

Ben —

We're seeing a sharp increase in inference latency and a spike in 5xx errors across our checkout flows starting ~08:45 PST. Our dashboard shows queue depth on the dedicated GPU pool for our account has grown 6x and reserved throughput isn't being honored — requests are getting queued for >2 seconds and some are failing. Impact: checkout latency >2s for 8% of requests, intermittent 502/504 errors, user-facing retries. This is causing order abandonment on a high-value flow. Please escalate — we need temporary capacity/burst or failover to hosted models while procurement sorts the PO.

Attached: hyperpay_error_snippets_0912.log, po_hold_notice.pdf

Ishaan Rao

Ben/Team —

Quick triage summary (10:00 AM):
- Cause: confirmed; the reservation delta means HyperPay's traffic was routed to shared headroom. Heavy tail of jobs + KV-cache warmup created sustained queue depth on the Dedicated farm (primarily p2/long-tail jobs).
- Immediate mitigation performed:
  * Opened emergency burst node group for HPAY (8 GPUs) — will be active for 4 hours (10:00–14:00 PST) and auto-shrink.
  * Applied soft-priority preemption policy on the affected hosts to favor reserved QPS from HPAY until burst drains.
  * Deployed traffic-split rule: 15% of checkout traffic rerouted to Redwood-hosted low-latency variant (verified for same model family, deterministic fallback).
- Observed effect (10:02): queue depth down ~70%, tail latency back to ~350ms for routed traffic; 5xx rate down by 60% on initial samples. Metrics exported to ops-sla-metrics-20271220.csv (attached).

Cost/authorization: bursting will consume ~1.6x of their typical daily GPU-credit burn for the 4-hour window. We need sales/finance signoff to bill as emergency consumption or apply a one-time credit.

Next steps:
- Ben/Marissa: confirm commercial handle (credit vs charge) — urgent.
- Ben/Ishaan: need confirmation of peak QPS to validate capacity sizing (we used conservative figure).
- Jordan: can you watch the KV cache hit rates and confirm no model-regression artifacts from the hosted variant?

I'll monitor for the next 30–60 minutes and tighten ramps if we see noisy neighbors.

—Olga
